sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Beast Claw** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Bestial Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Quest Item:** Bestial Sanctum, Greyoll's Dragonbarrow
- Beast Claw is rewarded from Gurranq after giving him the fifth Deathroot. (If Gurranq is hostile after consuming the fourth Deathroot, he may be calmed down by reducing his HP.)

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
Put a hand into the ground and swipe forwards to unleash a cone of shearing claws that have Slash Attack Power equal to 193% of Incantation Scaling.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 222% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 10 points of FP to cast.
- Costs 27 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases Stamina cost to 35 points.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot.
- Deals 7 Stance damage. Charging the spell increases Stance damage to 12.95.

sections.heading: Boosting
sections.markdown:
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon.
 - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 15%, this increases the Attack Power by a total of 32%.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- Slash is a very give-and-take damage type, as naked and cloth-wearing enemies (such as Omens and Margit, the Fell Omen) are weak or less resistant to the damage type, while armored and scaled or rock-like enemies (such as Banished Knights, Dragons, and Sentry Stones) are far more resistant to it than other Physical damage types.
- Can be jumped over.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Used by D, Hunter of the Dead, Gurranq, Beast Clergyman, Magnus the Beast Claw, and certain Vulgar Militia.
- Was wielded by the version of the Prophet found in the Elden Ring Closed Network Test.
- The Beast Claw has five "fingers", the signifier of a beast's intelligence.
- Patch 1.07: Increased the range of the shockwave.
- Patch 1.07: (Bug Fixes) Fixed a bug where recovery time after casting Beast Claw could not be shortened by magic or incantations.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Ashes of War** are special items in Elden Ring that can be used to modify the Skills of certain armaments, and (optionally) infuse them with one of a selection of possible Affinities. With any Whetblade, they can be applied to compatible armaments while resting at a Site of Grace, or by Smithing Master Hewg.

Ashes of War are not consumed when applied; rather, they are slotted into the armament, and can be removed at any time.

sections.heading: Usage & Application
sections.markdown:
Each Ash of War corresponds to a specific Skill, and can only be applied to armaments compatible with that skill; for instance, Ash of War: Piercing Fang can only be applied to weapons capable of thrusting attacks, but Ash of War: Kick can be applied to any melee weapon. Ashes of War also cannot be applied to any weapon that is upgraded using Somber Smithing Stones.

Ashes of War also each have a corresponding "native" Affinity; for instance, Ash of War: Bloody Slash has the Blood affinity. When being applied to an armament, this Affinity can optionally be infused to change the weapon's base damage values, damage scaling, and/or status effect buildups; alternatively, the armament can be left with the Standard affinity to keep the default scaling, and other affinities can be chosen if corresponding Whetblades are held.

Ashes of War can be freely removed from weapons — refunding the Ash and reverting the weapon to its default Skill — or directly transferred between weapons. They can also be duplicated by Hewg with Lost Ashes of War — whether in the inventory or already on a weapon — consuming them in the process.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Ashes of War are most commonly obtained as a drop from certain Teardrop Scarabs; however, they are sometimes contained in chests, sold by merchants, dropped by certain enemies such as Night's Cavalry or the unique Godrick Knight in Fort Haight, or occasionally are available as potential rewards from boss Remembrances — for example, Ash of War: Waves of Darkness from the Remembrance of the Naturalborn.

Additionally, some weapons have Ashes of War pre-equipped on acquisition, such that they can be applied to other weapons or duplicated from them. For example, the Nagakiba has Ash of War: Piercing Fang equipped on acquisition, despite having Unsheathe as its base skill when Piercing Fang is removed; and Backhand BladeShadow of the Erdtree has Ash of War: Blind Spot pre-equipped while simultaneously having Blind Spot as its underlying base skill. This often occurs when the Ash is otherwise impossible to obtain naturally.

sections.heading: Skill Scalings
sections.markdown:
It depends on the Ash of War individually if the Skill it grants scales with the weapon's attack rating, or your character's stats and the weapon's upgrades.

For example: Ash of War: Lion's Claw will deal over 1000 damage on a Keen-infused +25 Flamberge equipped to a character with 20str/40dex and less than 1000 if the Ash of War's default Heavy-infusion was chosen instead; meanwhile, Ash of War: Ground Slam will deal less damage if any infusion option other than Heavy is chosen, even if the weapon's attack rating would be higher with something else.

sections.heading: Number of Ashes
sections.markdown:
There are a total of 91 Ashes of War in the Elden Ring base game:

Standard 12, Keen 11, Quality 12, Lightning 3, Magic 10, Sacred 11, Heavy 14, Fire 3, Blackflame/Flame Art 2, Poison 2, Cold 3, Blood 4, Occult 4

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Bloody Finger Nerijus** is a mini-boss NPC invader in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: A member of the Bloody Fingers, Nerijus is a Tarnished driven mad by bloodlust and in service to Mohg, Lord of Blood.prowls along a shallow river in Limgrave, waiting to ambush Tarnished. When Nerijus attempting to ambush a Tarnished by invading them outside the cave, Yura, who knew him by name, came to the Tarnished's assistance.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.markdown:
Nerijus will spawn in Limgrave along the riverbed beneath the bridge where the Night's Cavalry spawns at night, just as one nears the Murkwater Cave entrance. Like other NPC invaders, when he arrives, the Tarnished will be unable to use Torrent, leave the immediate vicinity, or enter the cave. He'll spawn at the far end of the riverbed and start running towards the player.

It's recommended to either clear out all Those Who Live in Death near the bridge before spawning Nerijus, as they can be a nuisance while fighting him, You can also avoid them by keeping to the other end of the riverbed, closer to where Nerijus spawns in.

Nerijus is aggressive and armed with a pair of Reduvia daggers that give him a mix of quick ranged and melee attacks that all inflict bleed buildup. However, he is fairly easy to knock around with a two-handed or heavy weapon; his poise is low due to his light armor set. If needing assistance, run back towards the bridge area to buy some time for Bloody Finger Hunter Yura to spawn in, who'll help assist in fighting Nerijus, though he can still be killed by Nerijus. The two of you together can keep him stunlocked with ease.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - Bloody Finger Nerijus was named **Nerijus** in .

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Bloody Finger Hunter Yura** is an NPC character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: A ronin warrior in an iron kasa reminiscent of the straw hats worn in the Land of Reeds, Yura was a hunter of Mohg's Bloody Fingers. He understood the hidden dangers of Dragon Communion and was once close to Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger, a former Drake Knight for whom he harbored deep feelings. He wielded the unblockable Piercing Fang technique with deadly precision.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown:
Yura can first be found resting beneath a fallen ruin south of the Dragon-Burnt Ruins in Limgrave. He warns the Tarnished to stay away from Agheel Lake, where Flying Dragon Agheel roosts. However, he offers his aid if the player is brave enough to hunt the mighty dragon. If the Tarnished slays Agheel, Yura speaks of the island Church of Dragon Communion, and cautions against Dragon Communion's corrupting influence.

When the Tarnished is ambushed by Bloody Finger Nerijus on the Murkwater River, Yura intervenes to thwart the invasion. Later, Yura travels to the Academy of Raya Lucaria, where the Tarnished may repay his aid by assisting him against a Ravenmount Assassin. There, Yura urges them to avoid Eleonora, the deadliest of all Bloody Fingers.

Yura ultimately tracks Eleonora to the Second Church of Marika on the Altus Plateau. In their final battle, he suffers a mortal wound to sever the Bloody Finger from her hand. As the Tarnished arrives too late, Yura implores Eleonora to renounce the cessblood before dying in their presence.

After his death, Yura's body becomes host to Shabriri, who claims that Yura willingly surrendered his vessel.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
1. *(Optional)* Limgrave
 - The following two steps can be completed in either order. His dialogue will vary depending on where he is met first.
 - Yura can be found under a fallen Azula ruin near the Seaside Ruins site of grace, southwest of Agheel Lake. Exhaust his dialogue and his summon sign will appear in Agheel Lake to assist against Flying Dragon Agheel. Speak to him again after defeating Agheel for further dialogue.
 - Enter the Murkwater River, the ravine north of Agheel Lake, and head towards Murkwater Cave. Bloody Finger Nerijus will invade you. After fighting Nerijus for a while, Yura appears to assist you. After defeating Nerijus, continue along the ravine to find Yura under a bridge. Exhaust his dialogue.
1. Liurnia of the Lakes
 - A red summon sign can be found northeast of the Raya Lucaria Main Gate. Interact with it to assist Yura in defeating Bloody Finger Ravenmount Assassin. After defeating the foe, Yura can be found on the bridge near where the summon sign was. Speak to him to receive a [[item:smithing-stone-5|Smithing Stone [5]]].
1. Altus Plateau
 - Travel to the Second Church of Marika, located northwest of the Altus Highway Junction site of grace, where Yura lies on the ground. Speak to him, and then pick up the Nagakiba. Shortly after, Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger will invade. Defeat her to receive Eleonora's Poleblade and the Purifying Crystal Tear.
1. Mountaintops of the Giants
 - Once you travel to the Mountaintops of the Giants, Yura's quest will be locked regardless of which steps have been completed. Shabriri will be waiting near the Zamor Ruins site of grace, in possession of Yura's reanimated body. The Nagakiba can be found on the ground in whichever location he would have been at, depending on how far into his questline you have progressed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Wears the Ronin's Set: Iron Kasa, Ronin's Armor, Ronin's Gauntlets, and Ronin's Greaves.
- Wields a Nagakiba +7 with Ash of War: Piercing Fang equipped.
- After Yura's death, Shabriri possesses his body.

sections.markdown:

- Bloody Finger Hunter Yura replaced Redeemer Guilbert, a cut character from an early, prelease version of *Elden Ring*. Guilbert, also voiced by Shaun Dooley, initial stood in the same spot in which Yura now stands.

sections.markdown: Black Knife** is a melee armament found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: Received upon defeating the Black Knife Assassin in front of Sainted Hero's Grave located in Altus Plateau.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Technically leans towards a pure (80) Dexterity build with its scaling, but practically speaking a hybrid (45/45) Dexterity/Faith build gains about as much Attack Power (AP) while also making the skill stronger since it only scales with weapon upgrade level and the user's Faith.
 - Effectively, the hybrid build loses about 2% AP compared to the pure build (494 AP vs 503 AP) in exchange for gaining about 13% more AP for the initial hit of the skill (969 AP vs 856 AP).
- Despite its often resisted Holy damage this weapon still pulls its weight well due to the percentage-based damage effect its skill also causes, even when dodged through.
 - This health drain effect triggers even when rolled through so to fully avoid it can't be allowed to touch your body when dodged.
- Has a unique double-hitting heavy attack shared with the Blade of Calling, Erdsteel Dagger, and Fire Knight's Shortsword.
 - This unique attack grants 4 points towards the scaling of the Winged Sword Insignias instead of the usual 2 due to hitting twice.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.markdown:
- Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
- Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.
- See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Blaidd the Half-Wolf** is an NPC character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
A guarded and boorish yet fiercely loyal half-wolf, Blaidd was a shadowbound beast, created by the Two Fingers to serve Lunar Princess Ranni when she was chosen as an Empyrean. The wolf was the beast of the Carian royal covenant and irrefutably symbolized the moon's pride, and so he was approved and raised by Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon as Ranni's stepbrother.

Blaidd was Ranni's unwavering blade. Like all shadowbound beasts, he could not truly die and was incapable of treachery against his master, compelled to enact her will. Unbeknownst to him, however, an accursed failsafe within shadows overrode this directive should their master turn against the Two Fingers; should Ranni rebel against her prescribed fate, Blaidd’s unwavering loyalty would twist into madness, becoming a Baleful Shadow—a dire threat to Ranni herself.

When Blaidd swore an oath to serve no master other than Ranni the Witch and her Dark Moon, a cold frost magic graced his Royal Greatsword. The cold bothered him, nonetheless.

sections.heading: Game Events
sections.markdown: Blaidd searched the Mistwood Ruins for a traitor named Darriwil, and the passage to Nokron, Eternal City, a long-lost ruin said to be banished underground by the Greater Will. He travels to Redmane Castle to participate in the Radahn Festival.

 - Use Finger Snap at the Mistwood Ruins near the ruined tower adjacent to the slumbering Runebear to cause Blaidd to jump down. Talk to him and exhaust his dialogue.
1. Limgrave (Forlorn Hound Evergaol)
 - Enter the Forlorn Hound Evergaol in Limgrave and defeat Bloodhound Knight Darriwil. Blaidd will be available as a summonable cooperator during this fight.
 - After defeating Darriwil, Blaidd appears outside the Forlorn Hound Evergaol. Speak with him to earn a [[item:somber-smithing-stone-2|Somber Smithing Stone [2]]].
1. Liurnia of the Lakes (Ranni's Rise)
 - After entering Ranni's service, a projection of Blaidd appears in Ranni's Rise and offers dialogue. This step is skipped if Starscourge Radahn has already been defeated.
1. Siofra River
 - Blaidd moves to the base of an enormous ruined bridge on the bank of the Siofra River, located between the Siofra River Bank and Worshipper's Woods Sites of Grace. He will suggest asking Preceptor Seluvis about how to reach Nokron, Eternal City. This step is skipped if Starscourge Radahn has already been defeated.
 - (Optional) After speaking to Seluvis about Nokron and then speaking to Sorceress Sellen, return to Blaidd and exhaust his dialogue. He will move to Redmane Castle afterwards.
1. Caelid (Redmane Castle)
 - Blaidd will appear in the Redmane Castle Plaza when the Radahn Festival begins. He also appears as an optional summon in the fight against Starscourge Radahn.
1. Caelid (Wailing Dunes)

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Boc the Seamster** or **Demi-Human Boc** is an NPC in Elden Ring. He offers the player the ability to modify their garments, free of charge.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Boc is a demi-human seamster from Limgrave. He was very close to his mother, a seamstress, until her passing. Inspired by her, Boc aspired to follow in her footsteps and inherited her sewing kit. He lived with a demi-human tribe in a Coastal Cave on the western coast of Limgrave, but at some point, he was cast out by his kin. Lost and isolated, Boc was transformed into a bush by a spell.

A Tarnished came across Boc and broke the spell, freeing him. Grateful, Boc offered to sneak back into the cave where he had been exiled to retrieve something precious with which to repay his champion. However, his former tribe discovered him and beat him mercilessly. When the champion found Boc again, he warned them not to enter the cave. Ignoring his warning, the champion avenged Boc and recovered his mother's cherished sewing needle. Moved by their kindness, Boc vowed to become a seamster like his mother.

Boc next encounters the champion in Liurnia of the Lakes, where he humbly offers his services as the champion's personal seamster. He will trace the champion's footsteps, following them to the Altus Plateau and the Royal Capital. Boc remains in awe of his master, and as the Tarnished champion draws closer to the throne of the Elden Lord, Boc will begin to refer to them as a lord.

Even though Boc is given a golden needle worthy of a master seamster, allowing him to perform modifications to the grab of the demigods themselves, Boc remains terribly self-conscious and bothered by his appearance. He asks his master whether they think he is ugly and expresses an interest in being reborn by Queen Rennala. Should the Tarnished champion aid Boc in fulfilling his wish to be reborn, Boc will travel to the Academy of Raya Lucaria and will be reborn a human through her powers. However, like many of those reborn by Rennala, the process goes awry, and Boc dies shortly thereafter.

Instead, the Tarnished champion may find a Prattling Pate which speaks with the voice of Boc's deceased mother, and tells him he's beautiful. Upon hearing this, Boc will be contented and will continue faithfully serving his lord.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: Grants a Body Buff that decreases Magic damage taken by 60% (20% in PvP) for 70 seconds for caster and allies within a 6 meter radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 13 points of Stamina to cast.
- Overall a very strong defensive incantation, if one that comes a bit late and will most likely come after the Magic-heavy area of Liurnia of the Lakes, with only the Astels and Loretta being the major Magic damage bosses left.
- Since it doesn't actually apply a flat increase to damage negation, just the damage taken, the actual effective new damage negation (the one shown on the character screen) can be calculated with the following formula: 1 - (1 - (current Magic damage negation)/100) * (1 - 0.60).
 - As an example, if Magic damage negation before casting the incantation is 25.000 the result becomes this: 1 - (1 - 25.000/100) * (1 - 0.60) = 0.7, or 70.0% Magic damage negation.
 - Against other players, simply replace the 0.60 with 0.20 for a new end result of 40.0% Magic damage negation.
- Since it's effectively the damage taken that is reduced, the higher Magic damage negation stat a character has before casting the spell the less effective it may appear to be in the statistics.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Summons a red, spectral version of Maliketh's Black Blade, then jumps and spins forwards with the blade to hit for Holy Attack Power equal to 225% of Incantation Scaling while also sending out a wave with Holy Attack Power equal to 162% of Incantation Scaling.

If the incantation is used again immediately afterwards, the second sword's Attack Power is increased to 232% of Incantation Scaling while the beam's Attack Power is increased to 169% of Incantation Scaling for the second cast.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 44 points of Stamina to perform, with the follow-up costing the same amount of Stamina for a total of 88 points of Stamina if both parts are used.
- The sword part deals 9 Stance damage and the beam part deals 4 Stance damage.
- Both the sword itself and the wave it sends out can hit the same target at melee range, meaning that the first cast effectively can have Attack Power roughly equal to 387% of Incantation Scaling while the follow-up cast can have Attack Power equal to 401% of Incantation Scaling.
- The beam attack applies two debuffs: the first deals damage equal to 0.1% of the target's maximum HP + 1 every 0.1 seconds for 2 seconds (total damage equal to 2% of target's maximum HP + 20) while the second debuff lowers the target's maximum HP by 10% for 15 seconds, signified by a part of their health bar being blocked out with grey.
 - The debuff that lowers maximum HP doesn't stack with the Maliketh's Black Blade's skill Destined Death similar debuff, but it does stack with the one inflicted by the Black Knife's skill Blade of Death.

 - Black Blade is incorrectly referred to as Black Sword in this patch note.
- Patch 1.07.1 the incantation Black Blade is currently missing its follow up attack when cast from the left hand. This issue will be corrected in a future update.
 - The issue was fixed with Patch 1.08.
- Patch 1.07 reduced stamina consumption, improved turning performance and shortened recovery time, the sword and the wave attack have been changed so that they hit at the same time. Attack power, stamina attack power, and poise damage of each part have been decreased, decreased the number of times the wave part hits large enemies.
 - Prior to this only either the sword attack or the beam attack could hit an enemy.
 - The Attack Power of the first sword and beam was decreased from 290% of Incantation Scaling and 252% of Incantation Scaling to 225% and 162% of the same respectively, and the Attack Power of the follow-up sword and beam was decreased from 297% of Incantation Scaling and 260% of Incantation Scaling to 232% and 169% of the same respectively.

 - The Stamina damage to guarding players was split from the PvE values and increased at the same time, going to 181 and 143 for the first sword and beam, and to 200 and 156 for the follow-up sword and beam.
 - The Stance damage of sword attacks and beam attacks were decreased from 10 and 7 to 9 and 4 respectively. The Poise damage of sword attacks and beam attacks meanwhile was actually increased, not decreased, going from 100 and 70 to 243 and 108 respectively.
- Patch 1.04 decreased Stamina consumption and decreased recovery time.

- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Godslayer's Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- An very strong yet simple spell due to a combination of fast casting speed and percentage-based damage.
 - Since it deals at least 2% of a target's health per cast it can kill anything damageable in 50 casts, though most often much quicker due to the Fire damage it also deals.
- All bosses in Shadow of the Erdtree are resistant to the percentage-based damage of Blackflame, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. - Can have its extremely short duration extended by 30% by the Old Lord's Talisman, to 9.1 seconds.
- The Blackflame effect is also applied to target's hit by Skills of the buffed weapon, even if those skills don't involve the weapon, such as with Skill: Thunderbolt or Skill: Flame of the Redmanes.
- Casts considerably quicker if used immediately after a roll, jump, or attack, or when sprinting, letting the user get more out of its short duration.
- The additional damage from the Blackflame effect will at most be 9% of target's maximum HP + 90 (11.1% + 110 if the Old Lord's Talisman is used). Practically though, the bonus damage will probably be around 5% + 50, presuming the user is able to keep on the offense.
 - It's important to note that the duration of Blackflame effects doesn't stack, instead the duration is reset if another hit is landed during an ongoing burn.
 - Due to the extremely short duration of this buff, it's important to keep on the offensive if possible after casting the spell.
- Should ideally be cast just before an opening in a boss's attacks happens.
- Outmatched in added Fire Attack Power (i.e. not counting the added Blackflame effect) by Drawstring Fire Grease below 170 Incantation Scaling and by Drawstring Messmerfire Grease Shadow of the Erdtree below 208 Incantation Scaling.
 - Note that both of these consumable items last considerably longer than Black Flame Blade, even if the Old Lord's Talisman is equipped. More specifically, Drawstring Fire Grease lasts for 10 seconds and Drawstring Messmerfire Grease lasts for 25 seconds.
- Can be used with a quick weapon such as the Dagger, even if it's unupgraded, to deal heavy damage to high-health bosses.
- All bosses in Shadow of the Erdtree are resistant to the percentage-based damage of Blackflame, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler, Bayle the Dread, and the Promised Consort are even more resistant to the effect, only taking damage equal to 0.7% of target's maximum HP + 7.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Black Flame Ritual** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Godslayer Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Guaranteed Drop:** Mountaintops of the Giants
- Black Flame Ritual is received upon defeating the Spiritcaller Snail boss in Spiritcaller Cave on the Mountaintops of the Giants. This Snail summons the spirits of a Godskin Apostle and a Godskin Noble.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Summon a circle of Blackflame around the caster for about 4 seconds, hitting with Fire Attack Power equal to 106% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting an effect that deals damage equal to 2% of target's maximum HP + 20, over the course of 2 seconds, if an enemy touches them.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 109% of Incantation Scaling and creates the circle a bit further away from the caster.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 39 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 51 points.
- Deals 5 Stance damage per hit. Charging the spell increases the Stance damage to 6.5 per hit.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
 - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 3%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 18%.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Godslayer's Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- The ring can hit an enemy up to 4 times, effectively granting it Attack Power equal to 424% of Incantation Scaling (436% if charged), not accounting for flat defence, and dealing additional damage equal to 5% of target's maximum HP + 20 (since hitting with a new Blackflame effect will just reset the duration of the debuff).
 - This makes the incantation surprisingly usable for attacking, at least against large opponents such as Trolls, since enemies can be tricked into standing inside of the flames.
 - An older instance of Black Flame Ritual isn't removed when a new is cast, though their damage won't stack as efficiently against opponents compared to when their casts are more separated.
 - Significantly harder to use against other players, being primarily useful for forcing them to stay away from the caster or to obscure the caster's other attacks. Be wary of opponent's jumping over the flames or simply running through them, as well as the fact that the charged version's pillars being further out means it's possible to stand close to the caster without being damaged.
- All bosses in Shadow of the Erdtree are resistant to the percentage-based damage of Blackflame, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler, Bayle the Dread, and the Promised Consort are even more resistant to the effect, only taking damage equal to 0.7% of target's maximum HP + 7.

sections.heading: Acquisition

Purchase:** Roundtable Hold
- Acquired from Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing after selecting the "about the secret medallion" dialogue option. This option will only appear after the player has obtained both the Haligtree Secret Medallion (Right) and Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left).
- Can be purchased from the Twin Maiden Husks for 2,500 Runes should the player not talk to Gideon about both medallions before unleashing the Rune of Death.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: Grants a Body Buff that decreases Physical damage taken by 35% (15% in PvP) while also decreasing all healing received by 20% for 70 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 30 FP per cast.
- Costs 13 Stamina per cast.
- Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
- This spell reduces Physical damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where *PhysicalFortification* represents the effect magnitude:
 TotalPhysicalReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {PhysicalDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {PhysicalFortification}) ) 
 - For example, if physical damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
 PhysicalMagicReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.35) ) = 51.25% 
 - Against other players, the total reduction would be 36.25%:
 TotalPhysicalReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.15) ) = 36.25%

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- The reduction in healing effective lowers the effectiveness of this spell to only lowering Physical damage taken by 18.75% (and increasing the effective damage taken in PvP by 6.25%), assuming that healing will be used and not accounting for it helping the player survive hits that otherwise would have killed them.
 - Effectively still has its full PvP strength of 15% in no-healing scenarios such as semi-formal duels in the open world or via a Duelist's Furled Finger, and the Duel Arena Combat mode available through the Royal Colosseum in Leyndell, Royal Capital or via Roundtable Hold.
- The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as physical damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple physical negation sources.
- This incantation is valuable whenever available since the vast majority of areas will have most of the damage inflicted by enemies as various types of Physical damage. The biggest exception is Liurnia of the Lakes, where Magic damage shares the spotlight.
- Black Flame's Protection offers greater physical protection than Boiled Crab (35% vs. 20%) and has a slightly longer duration (70 vs. 60 seconds). This spell requires 30 Faith and 1 Memory Slot to be equipped and 30 FP to cast, while the Crab only requires 600 Runes per piece bought.
 - The Boiled Crab is preferable for PvP encounters, as Black Flame's Protection's effect is reduced to 15%.
 - Though Boiled Crab (and the slightly weaker Boiled Prawn) are potentially accessible much earlier, it's possible to not gain access to them should Blackguard Big Boggart be killed before any of either has been bought from him.
- The reduction in healing for the Flask of Crimson Tears specifically can be countered with either the Crimson Seed Talisman or Crimson Seed Talisman +1, setting healing effectiveness to 96% and 104% respectively.
 - Note that this only helps with the flask, as the Heal spells are not affected by either talisman but is affected by the healing reduction.

sections.markdown: Banished Knight Engvall** is a spirit ash in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: - Dropped by Grave Warden Duelist in Murkwater Catacombs.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Upgraded with Ghost Gloveworts.
- Summons a Banished Knight that wields a halberd with a more mobile variant of the Stormcaller skill on it.
- Deals Standard and Pierce damage.
- A slow, tanky summon that can hit decently hard and is available very early on, Engvall's main drawback is his huge FP cost which puts him out of range of most early builds that aren't focused on magic. This makes him an ideal companion for a caster that doesn't mind devoting all or most of a cerulean flask to him.
- Though he is quite durable, he is quite expensive, FP-wise, to summon. His halberd gives him wide-sweeping attacks for cleaving through crowds, while his Stormcaller has good AOE and can knock many enemies flat. Still, he is greatly outclassed by Banished Knight Oleg due to the latter's greater damage potential: Oleg tends to move and attack faster with in longer combos, while Engvall is a bit slower and also isn't quite as good at keeping foes staggered.
